_comment: Copy to triage-config.json and edit. This is the ONLY file you must customize to make the ATS pipeline work for your field. Patterns are JavaScript regex source strings, matched case-insensitively against the job title.
_salaryFloor: Hard minimum annual base in your currency. A posting whose feed-reported minimum is below this is rejected at zero cost. Postings with no stated salary are NOT rejected here; they pass to a later stage. Hourly, weekly and monthly ranges are converted to an annual figure before the comparison; a figure whose pay period the feed did not state is treated as no salary rather than guessed at.
_maxAgeDays: Reject postings older than this many days, using the date the feed reports. 0 turns the check off, which is the default: a cutoff set too tight quietly discards live roles, and government and academic hiring cycles routinely leave a real opening posted for months. If you set it, 60-90 is a sane starting point, and note that Greenhouse reports last-updated rather than first-posted, so its postings read younger than they are. A posting with no usable date is never rejected here.
_matchTitlePatterns: REPLACE THESE with the titles of your field. A title matching any of these becomes a 'match' and is worth pulling the full posting for. Be specific: these are what make the pipeline useful. Examples by field -- nursing: '\\bregistered\\s+nurse\\b'; software: '\\bbackend\\s+engineer\\b'; teaching: '\\bcurriculum\\s+(specialist|coordinator)\\b'.
_excludeTitlePatterns: Sub-professional tier and wrong-occupation rejects. The defaults here are field-agnostic and safe for most users. ADD your own for adjacent-but-wrong specialties that share your vocabulary -- these save the most tokens, because near-miss titles are exactly what a keyword search surfaces. Remove any that would reject roles you actually want (e.g. delete the 'seasonal' line if seasonal work suits you).
_genericTitlePattern: Titles too generic to judge alone. These become 'review' (not 'match') and only when the employer is in relevantSectors.
_relevantSectors: Sector tags from your ats-feeds.json. A generic title only reaches 'review' at an employer in one of these. Leave a sector OUT if its employers post hundreds of roles you never want -- that single change is the difference between a usable shortlist and a holding pen.
_locationHintPattern: Locations you can work without extra steps (visa, relocation). A domain-title match OUTSIDE this becomes 'review' rather than 'match', so it surfaces but is flagged. Non-US users: replace with your own country/region pattern.
